# horizontal + vertical scroll looks bad on chrome

A user reports that when a scrollable region ends up showing a horizontal and a
vertical scrollbar at the same time, it renders badly in Chrome and looks out of
place against the rest of the UI. The problem is visible on load — no interaction
is needed to reproduce it.

They attached a screenshot of what they saw:

![Screenshot attached to the report, showing the problem in Chrome](/app/.harbor_assets/bug.png)

Please look at the screenshot to determine exactly what is rendering incorrectly,
then fix it so the affected area no longer looks out of place.

The screenshot shows the Automator command list with both a horizontal and vertical scrollbar. The red circle highlights the **scrollbar corner** (the small square where the two scrollbars meet) — in Chrome it renders as a bright white box, which clashes with the dark themed UI around it.

Let me find the relevant styling in the codebase.

The global scrollbar CSS at the top of `styles.css` styles the scrollbar track and thumb, but never styles `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner`. In Chrome, that corner (where the horizontal and vertical scrollbars intersect) defaults to an opaque white box — exactly the bright square circled in the screenshot. It stands out against the dark UI.

Let me confirm there's no existing corner rule anywhere:

Confirmed — there's no `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` rule anywhere. Chrome fills that corner with the default opaque white, which is the out-of-place white square in the screenshot. The `::-webkit-scrollbar` track itself has no background set (so it's transparent), but the corner is a separate pseudo-element that must be styled explicitly.

I'll add a corner rule alongside the existing global scrollbar styles so it blends with the transparent track:

content.text:
## What was wrong

In the screenshot, the scrollable Automator command list showed a horizontal and a vertical scrollbar at once. Where they meet in the bottom-right corner, Chrome painted a bright **white square** (the circled area) — glaringly out of place against the dark themed track and UI.

That corner is the `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` pseudo-element. Chrome renders it as an opaque white box by default, and the stylesheet styled the scrollbar track and thumb but never the corner — so whenever both scrollbars appear together, the white default showed through.

## The fix

Added a `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` rule (in `public/stylesheets/styles.css`, next to the existing global scrollbar styles) setting its background to `transparent`, matching the already-transparent track. The corner now blends into the surrounding UI instead of showing a white block.

```css
::-webkit-scrollbar-corner {
  background: transparent;
}
```

This is a global rule, so it fixes the corner everywhere both scrollbars co-occur, not just the Automator pane. The problem is visible on load with no interaction, consistent with the report, since it's purely a static styling gap.
